text:
alex: FYI seeing sustained read IOPS surge in us-central2 nvme pool shard-7 — GPU allocation queue climbing, some binds failing. Anyone touching janitor or scrub cadence? :eyes:
maria: Which graph? node id sample?
alex: snippet from metrics:
```
[node=us-central2-nvme-7] read_iops=456k write_iops=22k avg_lat=14ms fsync_backlog=120 pending_allocs=200
```
tian: That pattern looks like janitor overlap + a possible firmware requeue. We rolled janitor cadence last night in us-central2. @ryan did you change concurrency?
ryan: I rolled a faster cadence at 02:12 UTC — concurrency 4->8 to catch up. Checking rollout logs now.
infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_iops_spike detected us-central2 at 2025-11-02T02:48:01Z — auto-tagged storage-team
maria: Doubling concurrency explains it. Temp fix: scale janitor concurrency back to 2 and pause aggressive scrub jobs on hot shards. Quick patch command:
```
PATCH /infra/api/v1/configs/janitor -d '{"concurrency":2, "hot_shard_pause":true}'
```
alex: Applied to canary at 1755004389 (3 nodes). IOPS dropped to ~160k after ~6m. pending_allocs still ~140.
tian: Next: cordon top-2 hottest nodes and drain GPUs so cleaners can finish without producing more small reads. Also add routing rule to steer new gpu-allocs away from this nvme pool to ssd-fallback for a few hours.
maria: Opening rollback ticket for the cadence change and creating follow-up to capture wear-rate + SMART anomalies across affected drives. Added incident board: https://redwood.infra/boards/IOPS-1755 :thumbsup:
alex: Will watch pending_allocs. Ping if it crosses 200 again. :coffee:
